And how did he react to that?
He was very surprised and upset.
I even felt a little sorry for him.
Just do not tell anyone the truth.
Of course, no one will find out anything.
Thank you, you are a true loyal friend!
Listen, maybe we should go somewhere?
Where exactly do you suggest going?
Let us go to the movies together.
This is needed for the believability of our plan.
Great idea, let us go tonight!
Agreed, then let us meet after work.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

examples.text: Ты мой главный учитель и верный наставник.
examples.trans: You are my main teacher and true mentor.

examples.text: А я вообще очень верная женщина.
examples.trans: And I am actually a very loyal woman.

meanings.note: до вечера = until the evening; вечером = in the evening

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'together' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы с Пашей вместе уже месяц.
examples.trans: Pasha and I have been together for a month now.

examples.text: Аркаша, губернатор хочет с нами встретиться!
examples.trans: Arkasha, the governor wants to meet with us!

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: Core Russian part meaning 'even' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.en: to agree, to come to an arrangement

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

жалко.gloss: feel sorry for; it's a pity

meanings.note: impersonal predicate (+ dative of experiencer, + accusative/genitive)

examples.trans: I just feel sorry for him.

examples.text: Что за глупость? Эдик, мне его просто жалко.
examples.trans: What nonsense is that? Edik, I just feel sorry for him.
Edik, I just feel sorry for him.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'быть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forget', paired with 'забывать'.

examples.trans: Don't forget to wash the toilet.

examples.text: Сейчас будешь чинить трубу. И унитаз не забудь помыть.
examples.trans: Now you're going to fix the pipe. And don't forget to wash the toilet.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'idea' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Хорошая идея! Я сейчас же попробую.
examples.trans: Good idea! I will try right now.

meanings.note: вот именно = that's just it, quite right

examples.text: Именно это я и хотел сказать.
examples.trans: That is justamente what I wanted to say.

examples.text: Вот именно. Но мне сдаваться нельзя.
examples.trans: Exactly. But I must not give up.

meanings.note: как вы знаете = as you know

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?
Then invite me to the movies.
So, let's look at the schedule in the cinema.

examples.text: Зачем ты вообще ведёшь её в кино?
examples.trans: Why are you even taking her to the movies?

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: for movement; где is for location

examples.trans: Wait, where are you two going?

examples.text: Куда-нибудь, шеф меня только что уволил.
examples.trans: Anywhere, the chef just fired me.

examples.text: Слушай, а может мы сходим куда-нибудь?
examples.trans: Listen, maybe we should go somewhere?

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').

examples.text: Ваня, да пойми ты наконец! Это настоящий успех.
examples.trans: Vanya, understand at last! This is real success.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to do a bit of work.

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.
examples.trans: We are giving you a little more time.

meanings.note: needs 'не' with the verb: никто не войдёт

examples.trans: I know the town like nobody else.

examples.text: Садитесь и держите дверь. Никто не войдёт.
examples.trans: Sit down and hold the door. Nobody will come in.

meanings.note: usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: short form 'нужен / нужна / нужно / нужны' + dative: 'мне нужна работа' = I need a job
accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'личный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('excellent').

examples.text: Квартира будет отличная. На Симашко есть новый дом.
examples.trans: It'll be an excellent flat. There's a new building on Simashko Street.

examples.text: И как он на это отреагировал?
examples.trans: And how did he react to that?
I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'plan' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The mayor came up with a new plan.

examples.text: Но мэр придумал новый план. Сосед мэра теперь пойдёт в мэры.
examples.trans: But the mayor came up with a new plan. The mayor's neighbour will now run for mayor.
Can I go and have a look?

examples.text: Он за мной после концерта ухаживал.
examples.trans: He courted me after a concert once.

meanings.note: as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine
as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'plausibility, believability' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это нужно для правдоподобности нашего плана.
examples.trans: This is needed for the believability of our plan.
So, tell me, how are you doing?

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'строиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get upset', paired with 'расстраиваться'.

examples.text: Он очень сильно удивился и расстроился.
examples.trans: He was very surprised and upset.

meanings.note: + infinitive: решил стать = decided to become

examples.text: Суд решил: домашний арест по месту прописки.
examples.trans: The court has decided: house arrest at his registered address.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.
The wind is blowing hard outside.

examples.text: Я так два года потеряла. Любила так сильно!
examples.trans: I lost two years like that. I loved him so much!

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: the imperative 'слушай' starts a sentence, like 'look, ...'

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

examples.text: Ты слишком сентиментальным стал. А лидер должен быть жёстким.
examples.trans: You've become too sentimental. And a leader has to be tough.

meanings.en: to go and come back, to pop over

examples.trans: Yes, go on. Don't mix it up with another one!

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

удивиться.gloss: to be surprised, to be amazed

examples.trans: Just wait and see, you'll be surprised yet!
I was very surprised by his words.

examples.text: Я сам удивился, когда ощипывал его.
examples.trans: I was surprised myself when I was plucking it.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'знать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to recognise; to find out', paired with 'узнавать'.

examples.trans: I'll find out where he is.
You recognised me. Thanks for seeing me.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
